documents.unit: Learning Design Center / University AI guidance
documents.title: AI Use Policy and Guidance
documents.summary: University guidance covering teaching, research and administration. It mostly protects data, requires accountable, verified and disclosed AI use, names Gemini and NotebookLM as the preferred tools, and leaves academic permissions to instructors and programs.
documents.stance_why: The page does not itself allow or ban student AI use: "The use of generative AI in academic work is governed by USD’s academic integrity expectations and any additional requirements established by the instructor or academic program". It sets only data, accountability and disclosure expectations and leaves academic decisions to instructors.

units.why: The opening says "USD will review and update this guidance as the technology and regulatory environment develop", a commitment to revise, so it is a revisit-regularly policy (P54).
units.anchor: will review and update this guidance as the technology and regulatory environment develop

units.why: "USD supports the thoughtful, ethical, and responsible use of artificial intelligence" in teaching, research and administration is the institution-level statement of purpose and scope, so P56 rather than P116 since it frames the whole guidance.
units.anchor: supports the thoughtful, ethical, and responsible use of artificial intelligence in teaching, learning, research

units.why: "AI use remains subject to all existing university policies and procedures" lists data security, integrity, copyright and more; it ties AI to existing rules (P77).
units.anchor: AI use remains subject to all existing university policies and procedures

units.why: "Using AI does not replace or bypass established review and approval processes" and the example list (General Counsel review, public-facing materials) require users to keep following review processes; closest type is P77.
units.anchor: Using AI does not replace or bypass established review and approval processes.
units.fit_note: Specific to review and approval workflows (General Counsel, official materials), not only compliance with laws or policies.

units.why: "Academic work remains subject to course, program, and academic integrity requirements" says academic AI use is governed by existing course and integrity rules, so P77; it is not a new stance.
units.anchor: Academic work remains subject to course, program, and academic integrity requirements.

units.why: "Research remains subject to applicable institutional, sponsor, privacy, and compliance requirements" defers research AI use to sponsor and compliance rules, which is the P62 definition.
units.anchor: Research remains subject to applicable institutional, sponsor, privacy, and compliance requirements.

units.why: "Public-facing and official university materials must follow existing approval processes" governs AI in operational communications rather than teaching, so P76.
units.anchor: Public-facing and official university materials must follow existing approval processes.

units.why: "AI-generated materials must be reviewed by a USD employee before they are used for university business" requires human review of AI-made materials, matching P48 at the institution level.
units.anchor: AI-generated materials must be reviewed by a USD employee before they are used
units.fit_note: Covers all university business, not only course materials, and does not mention disclosure.

units.why: "The person using AI remains responsible for the final work and for any decisions made using it" makes the user answerable for output, which is P29.
units.anchor: The person using AI remains responsible for the final work

units.why: Before using an AI tool users must "consider the type of information involved and whether the tool is approved for that use", a data-protection and vetted-tools rule (P50).
units.anchor: consider the type of information involved and whether the tool is approved for that use
units.frag_start: Before using an AI tool, consider

units.why: The passage says information shared "may include prompts, uploaded files, personal identifiers" and that "Providers differ in how they protect, retain, use, and share this information"; it informs about data risk, P50.
units.anchor: Providers differ in how they protect, retain, use, and share this information.

units.why: University information may be used with an AI tool "only when" it is public or the tool is approved for that information type; this limits tools by data type (P50 vetted tools).
units.anchor: may use university information with an AI tool only when

units.why: "Access to an approved tool does not mean that every type of information or every proposed use is permitted" limits approved-tool use and tells users to check data allowances; P50 nearest.
units.anchor: Access to an approved tool does not mean that every type of information

units.why: "Gemini is the designated platform for approved uses involving non-public university information" and USD adopts Google AI as its "preferred and recommended AI toolkit"; this names institution-wide licensed tools, P92 (not P17, which is course-specific).
units.anchor: as its preferred and recommended AI toolkit.
units.frag_start: The University of San Diego has adopted

units.why: Gemini "may be used with approved content" in Gmail, Calendar and Drive when accessed via a USDOne account; a permission for a specific tool under data rules, P92.
units.anchor: Gemini may be used with approved content in USD’s Google Workspace environment
units.frag_start: When accessed through a USDOne account

units.why: "Gemini and NotebookLM may assist with tasks such as drafting, summarizing, comparing, organizing, and analyzing university materials" lists permitted uses; P59 fits only partly because it is not limited to teaching.
units.anchor: may assist with tasks such as drafting, summarizing, comparing, organizing, and analyzing university materials
units.fit_note: Applies to any university materials and all users, not specifically instructors' teaching work.

units.why: "Users must still verify the resulting content" tells users to check Gemini output, which is P31.
units.anchor: Users must still verify the resulting content and follow all applicable review

units.why: "Public or unapproved AI tools may be used only with information that is appropriate for public disclosure" restricts unapproved tools to public data, P50.
units.anchor: Public or unapproved AI tools may be used only with information that is appropriate

units.why: "Do not enter, upload, or connect: Student names, identification numbers, grades..." forbids putting records and non-public information into public AI tools, a data-protection ban; P50 fits, P49 covers only course materials.
units.anchor: Do not enter, upload, or connect: Student names, identification numbers, grades
units.frag_start: Do not enter, upload, or connect:

units.why: "These restrictions also apply to connectors, browser extensions, plug-ins, custom assistants, and third-party services" extends the data rule to AI embedded in extensions and integrations, P07.
units.anchor: These restrictions also apply to connectors, browser extensions, plug-ins, custom assistants
units.fit_note: Extends the data restriction to add-ons and integrations; does not address coding editors or student coursework.

units.why: "Treat anything entered into a public or unapproved AI tool as though it could become publicly accessible" warns about exposure, P50.

units.why: "Before using any AI service, review its current privacy, data-retention, model-training, security, and acceptable-use terms" asks users to assess a tool before use, P117.
units.anchor: review its current privacy, data-retention, model-training, security, and acceptable-use terms
units.frag_start: Before using any AI service, review

units.why: "You are fully responsible for work produced with the assistance of AI" makes users own AI-assisted work, P29.
units.anchor: You are fully responsible for work produced with the assistance of AI.
units.frag_start: You are fully responsible for work

units.why: "AI-generated content may be inaccurate, biased, incomplete, fabricated, outdated" and the list "Evaluate it critically. Verify factual claims..." tell users to verify output; P31.
units.anchor: Verify factual claims, quotations, calculations, citations, and references.

units.why: "Review it for bias, harmful assumptions, and accessibility" asks users to check output for bias; closest is P53 (naming bias), though it is an action step.
units.anchor: Review it for bias, harmful assumptions, and accessibility.
units.fit_note: An instruction to check output for bias and accessibility rather than a statement of concerns.

units.why: "Use AI to enhance—not replace—your thinking, expertise, learning, and decision-making" keeps the human as the thinker, P32.
units.anchor: Use AI to enhance—not replace—your thinking, expertise, learning, and decision-making.

units.why: "Be transparent when AI makes a meaningful contribution" and "Cite or disclose AI-generated content" require disclosure of material AI contributions, P24.
units.anchor: Be transparent when AI makes a meaningful contribution to academic, research

units.why: "Identify the AI tool used. Explain how it was used." lists what a disclosure should contain, tool and use details, P25.
units.anchor: Identify the AI tool used.
units.policy: Identify the AI tool used. Explain how it was used.
units.fit_note: Asks for tool and manner of use, but not the exact prompt or output.

units.why: "Follow the requirements established by the instructor, academic program, publisher, research sponsor, professional field, or responsible university office" defers disclosure rules to local authorities, P04.
units.anchor: Follow the requirements established by the instructor, academic program, publisher
units.fit_note: Also names publishers, sponsors and offices, not only instructors.

units.why: "consider who may be helped, harmed, included, or excluded by the use of AI" asks the community to weigh ethical effects, P118.
units.anchor: consider who may be helped, harmed, included, or excluded by the use of AI.
units.frag_start: As a Changemaker campus, USD also

units.why: "avoid using AI to mislead, discriminate, manipulate, or misrepresent" is a general conduct rule against deceptive use, P74.
units.anchor: avoid using AI to mislead, discriminate, manipulate, or misrepresent.
units.fit_note: Sits beside prompts to respect privacy and challenge biased outputs; the ban on misleading or discriminatory use is the type assigned.

units.why: "The use of generative AI in academic work is governed by USD’s academic integrity expectations and any additional requirements established by the instructor or academic program" sets no default and leaves decisions to instructors and programs, P04.
units.anchor: any additional requirements established by the instructor or academic program
units.frag_start: The use of generative AI in academic

units.why: "Review the AI expectations for each course and assignment" tells students to learn the rules for each course, P78.
units.anchor: Review the AI expectations for each course and assignment.

units.why: "Ask the instructor when permitted uses are unclear" is the ask-when-unsure rule, P10.
units.anchor: Ask the instructor when permitted uses are unclear.

units.why: "Cite or disclose AI use when required" is a conditional disclosure duty for students, P24.
units.anchor: Cite or disclose AI use when required.

units.why: "Avoid submitting AI-generated work as their own" says students should not hand in AI output as theirs, P19; the modality is should-not as written.
units.anchor: Avoid submitting AI-generated work as their own.

units.why: "Ensure that AI does not replace the learning or skill development an assignment is intended to support" asks students to protect the assignment's learning purpose, P41.
units.anchor: Ensure that AI does not replace the learning or skill development an assignment
units.frag_start: Ensure that AI does not replace

units.why: "Faculty should clearly communicate whether and how AI may be used" is an expectation on instructors to state AI rules, P09.
units.anchor: Faculty should clearly communicate whether and how AI may be used
units.policy: Faculty should clearly communicate whether and how AI may be used

units.why: "explain how those expectations relate to the assignment's learning outcomes" asks faculty to tie AI rules to learning outcomes, P83.
units.anchor: explain how those expectations relate to the assignment’s learning outcomes.

units.why: "Researchers should confirm that the selected tool is approved for the data involved and consult the appropriate research or compliance office" gives researchers a tool-approval and data duty, P62.
units.anchor: Researchers should confirm that the selected tool is approved for the data involved

units.why: The research bullets list human subjects, IRB, sponsor restrictions, authorship and reproducibility that govern AI use; P62.

units.fit_note: Phrased as a warning that upload may violate copyright, not a flat prohibition, and applies to all users.

units.why: Library databases are "governed by agreements that restrict copying, automated analysis, text and data mining, or use with generative AI" and misuse may "jeopardize access"; this is licensing and copyright, P52.

units.frag_start: Before using copyrighted or licensed material
units.frag_end: provider may retain or reuse the material.
units.policy: Confirm that the proposed use is permitted. Review the terms governing the source, database, or resource.

units.why: "Contact Copley Library if you are unsure whether a resource may be uploaded" points users to a human office for licensed-resource questions, P72.
units.anchor: Contact Copley Library if you are unsure whether a resource may be uploaded
units.fit_note: Directs users to the library about licensing, not to help with learning.

units.why: "this guidance cannot anticipate every situation" says the guidance is incomplete because AI changes quickly; P54 on provisional policy fits best.

units.why: "Ask your instructor about academic use" under "When in Doubt" is another ask-first rule, P10.

units.why: "Review the Approved AI Tools and Data Allowances" points users to a list of approved tools and data rules, P115 (further guidance).
units.anchor: Approved AI Tools and Data Allowances

units.why: "Contact Information Technology Services about security, integrations, connectors, or tool approval" names ITS as the office for tool approval questions, P80.

documents.title: MS in Applied Artificial Intelligence Graduate Student Handbook 2026-2027
documents.summary: The MS Applied AI handbook has a short Generative AI Guidelines section asking students to disclose use, verify output and treat AI as a learning aid, not a replacement. It also carries the school's general academic-integrity procedure.
documents.stance_why: The handbook says "You are encouraged to use ChatGPT and similar programs as a tool to support your own learning and critical thinking" subject to disclosure and verification, with no ban or tiers, so AI is permitted with conditions.

units.why: The handbook says "you must be transparent about your use and disclose any generated content as being produced by an AI program", a mandatory disclosure duty, P24.
